text.p: The following is a digest of stories reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Joint Baltic American National Committee reminded the United States once again that they expect concrete actions from the U.S. and that the path of Baltic countries to NATO goes via Washington.
- Progress was made on an agreement to readmit illegal immigrants beteween Belarus and Lithuania during the visit of Belarus foreign affairs minister Ivan Antonovich on Monday.

- According to the results of a Vilmora opinion poll, 31.2 percent of those surveyed would re-elect Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas if an election were held now. Some 21.8 percent would support Lithuanian-American Valdas Adamkus and 9.7 percent would vote for parliamentary chairman Vytautas Landsbergis. The ruling Homeland Union party led the pack with 16.5 percent of support followed by the Centre Union at 10.7 percent and the Lithuanian Democratic Labor Party at 6.6 percent. The Christians Democrats and Social Democrats each had the support of 6.3 percent of voter, the poll showed.
- Marijampoles Grain decided to boost its share capital by 2.5 million litas. It was the only way to save the financially troubled company, the head of the company A. Balaika said.
- Swedish press reports say that the Lithuanian Sea Shipping company intends to open a cargo and passenger ferry route between Klaipeda and Ahus in May.
- Lithuania commemorated the seventh anniversary of the restoration of country's independence on Tuesday.

- Latvian foreign affairs minister Valdis Birkavs has invited his Lithuanian counterpart Algirdas Saudargas to Riga for a one-day visit. Relations between the two countries have been soured by a disputed zone in the Baltic Sea.
- The state debt was $320 per capita in Lithuania on January 1, 1997, the statistics department said.
- The average monthly salary in Lithuania fell 7.8 percent in January to 687 litas.
- Lithuania is represented by 25 embassies and eight consulate offices abroad. Twenty-three countries have opened their diplomatic offices in Vilnius during the last seven years.
- Lithuanian Investment agency polled 46 foreign investors and 83 percent of the respondents said they would invest in Lithuania again.
- Lithuanian insurance companies collected 184.5 million litas in payments from customers in 1996, a 20.8 percent increase over the previous year.
- Inflation in February was 0.6 percent in Lithuania versus 0.4 percent in Latvia and 0.9 percent in Estonia.
